source.text: tantrasāra, dvitīyam āhnikam atha anupāyam eva tāvat vyākhyāsyāmaḥ // abhts_2.1 yadā khalu dṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhaḥ svayam eva itthaṃ vivecayati sakṛd eva guruvacanam avadhārya tadā punar upāyavirahito nityoditaḥ asya samāveśaḥ // abhts_2.2 atra ca tarka eva yogāṅgam iti kathaṃ vivecayati iti cet ucyate yo 'yaṃ parameśvaraḥ svaprakāśarūpaḥ svātmā tatra kim upāyena kriyate na svarūpalābho nityatvāt na jñaptiḥ svayaṃprakāśamānatvāt nāvaraṇavigamaḥ āvaraṇasya kasyacid api asaṃbhavāt na tadanupraveśaḥ anupraveṣṭuḥ vyatiriktasya abhāvāt // abhts_2.3 kaś cātra upāyaḥ tasyāpi vyatiriktasya anupapatteḥ tasmāt samastam idam ekaṃ cinmātratattvaṃ kālena akalitaṃ deśena aparicchinnam upādhibhir amlānam ākṛtibhir aniyantritaṃ śabdair asaṃdiṣṭaṃ pramāṇair aprapañcitaṃ kālādeḥ pramāṇaparyantasya svecchayaiva svarūpalābhanimittaṃ ca svatantram ānandaghanaṃ tattvaṃ tad eva ca aham tatraiva antar mayi viśvaṃ pratibimbitam evaṃ dṛḍhaṃ viviñcānasya śaśvad eva pārameśvaraḥ samāveśo nirupāyaka eva tasya ca na mantrapūjādhyānacaryādiniyantraṇā kācit // abhts_2.4

l1_text:
## tsa02-p01
Now we shall expound the means-less itself first. (2.1) When one pierced by firm descent, by himself, thus discriminates — having heeded the teacher's word just once — then, means-devoid, ever-risen is his immersion. (2.2) Here: "reason itself is the yoga-limb" — thus, how does he discriminate? If asked, it is said: this Lord, self-light-natured, is own self. Therein, what is done by means? Not attainment of nature — from eternity; not notification — from self-shiningness; not removal of covering — since covering of any kind is impossible; not entry into it — since there is no distinct enterer. (2.3) And what means here? Of it too, as distinct, there is impossibility. Hence: all this is one consciousness-only reality — unmeasured by time, undelimited by place, unfaded by attributes, uncontrolled by forms, unindicated by words, unelaborated by valid means — and the cause, by own will alone, of the attainment of own nature from time to valid means; autonomous, bliss-dense reality. And that itself am I; and therein, within me, the universe is reflected. For one thus firmly discriminating, ever is there Lordly immersion, means-less itself; and for it there is no constraint at all — by mantra, worship, meditation, or conduct. (2.4)
l2_text:
## tsa02-p01 — no means
First of the four ways in: the way with no way. When grace has struck firm, a person hears the teacher's word once — and then discriminates for himself. From that point his immersion needs nothing and never sets. Here "yoga-limb" means one thing only: thinking it through. But what is there to think? The Lord, who is self-shining, is yourself. So what could a means do? It can't get you your nature — you have it eternally. It can't inform you — you shine already. It can't strip a covering — there is none. It can't take you inside — there's no outsider to go in. And the means itself, as something separate from you, is equally impossible. So: all this is one reality, consciousness and nothing else — time can't measure it, place can't bound it, qualities can't fade it, shapes can't rule it, words can't point it out, proofs can't build it up. By its own will it is what lets everything from time to proof arrive at its nature; free, thick bliss; and that is I, with the universe mirrored inside me. Who sees this steadily is immersed in the Lord always, without means — no mantra binds him, no worship, no sitting, no observance.
*Fidelity: preserved (occasion, four impossibilities, six negations, identity + reflection, no-constraint close). Added: "thinking it through" for tarka (register); "thick bliss" for ānandaghana. Not-resolved: none.*

c1.body:
The first of the four ways in: the way with no way. When grace has struck firm, a person hears the teacher's word once and then discriminates for himself; from that point his immersion needs nothing and never sets. The question "how does he discriminate?" is answered by four impossibilities: no nature to attain (eternal), nothing to notify (self-shining), no covering to remove (none possible), no one to enter (no distinct enterer). The means itself, as something separate, is equally impossible. Hence all is one consciousness-only reality — unmeasured by time, undelimited by place, unfaded by attributes, uncontrolled by forms, unindicated by words, unelaborated by valid means — whose own will is the cause of nature-attainment from time to proof; autonomous, bliss-dense; "I am that, with the universe mirrored in me." Who sees this steadily is immersed in the Lord always, without means — no mantra, worship, meditation, or conduct binds him.

The passage moves in three steps, each removing a supposed need for means. First, the occasion: firm-descent-pierced, one heeds the teacher's word once, then self-discriminates — and immersion follows, means-devoid, ever-risen. The "heeds once" is crucial: no repetition, no practice, no gradual approach; the descent itself does the work. Second, the four impossibilities: attainment of nature (nityatvāt — you have it eternally, so nothing to gain), notification (svayaṃprakāśamānatvāt — you shine already, so nothing to inform), covering-removal (āvaraṇasya asaṃbhavāt — no covering exists to strip), entry (anupraveṣṭuḥ abhāvāt — no outsider to go inside). Plus the means itself as a distinct entity (anupapatteḥ — a separate means is equally impossible). Third, the positive: six negations of the consciousness-only reality (unmeasured by time, undelimited by place, unfaded by attributes, uncontrolled by forms, unindicated by words, unelaborated by valid means); own-will as the cause of nature-attainment from time to proof; autonomous; bliss-dense; "I am that, with the universe mirrored in me." Then the no-constraint close: no mantra, worship, meditation, or conduct binds him.
c1.terms: anupāya (means-less), samāveśa (immersion), nityodita (ever-risen), cinmātratattva (consciousness-only reality), svātantrya (autonomy), ānandaghana (bliss-dense), tarka (reason), vimarśa (grasping).
c1.see_also: A01 (svabhāva), A03 (śāmbhava), essay0 Q4 ("How do I see this?"), spans TS2.1–2.4.
c1.function: Establishes the first (anupāya) of the four upāyas. Argues that means presuppose lack, hiddenness, or distance — all impossible for self-light.
c1.local_context: Follows A01 (svabhāva); the four upāyas (anupāya/śāmbhava/śākta/āṇava) are previewed there and taught in A02–A05.
c1.boundary: The four impossibilities are Abhinava's own (Tantrasāra's condensation), not Utpaladeva's. The "I am that" identity claim is the ahnika's thesis. The other three upāyas follow (A03–A05).
